headline: U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) has issued a fact check in response to renewed Iranian claims that the Strait of Hormuz has been closed, stating that the claim is false. According to CENTCOM, commercial shipping continues to transit the waterway, which remains open despite the ongoing conflict. The command noted that Iran does not control the entire strait and that thousands of commercial vessels have successfully transited since the war began. Before the war, the Strait of Hormuz averaged approximately 130 commercial vessel transits per day. Since February 28, roughly 19,900 transits would have been expected under normal conditions. Instead, daily traffic has generally remained at around 10% of pre-war levels, with only occasional surges. The majority of commercial traffic has continued to use Iran's designated shipping channel, while an unknown number of vessels have instead transited via the U.S. established maritime safety corridor through Omani waters. Several vessels using that route have subsequently come under Iranian attack, underscoring that while the strait remains open, commercial shipping continues to operate in a high-threat environment.

headline: President Donald J. Trump announced that the Board of Peace has reached what he described as a "historic" agreement for the complete disarmament of Hamas and all other armed groups in Gaza. The Board of Peace is a U.S.-led international organization established earlier this year to oversee post-conflict stabilization, reconstruction, and governance in Gaza under Trump's broader peace plan. According to Trump, the agreement will be implemented in phases, with Hamas disarming, Israeli forces withdrawing as benchmarks are met, and an International Stabilization Force working alongside a new Palestinian police force under a new Palestinian government. Trump also credited Egypt, Qatar, and Turkey for their mediation efforts, calling the agreement a major milestone in his 20-Point Plan and stating that Gaza "will no longer be used as a base for terror attacks."
